first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates shortened, simplified onboarding improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. This directly addresses two current headwinds and is more likely to create durable qualified revenue than broadly discounting. Verify the onboarding and pricing source records before commitment because competitor pricing makes the acquisition trade-off material; test onboarding first with qualified-revenue and retention guardrails.

final.rationale: Run a standard, guarded onboarding-simplification experiment. The verified prior result directly addresses both current declines: onboarding completion rose 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention rose 3%. Signup simplification also previously lifted SMB first-week activation. This is a more sustainable route to qualified revenue than promotional pricing, whose verified cohort showed 12% lower 30-day retention despite acquisition lift. Monitor qualified-account rate, activation, 30-day retention, and any loss of sales qualification data as guardrails.
